brief: Bloomberg strategist Frank Monkam argues volatility is forming a higher floor even as underlying assets correct: 10-year yields fell over 40bp from early-October highs to ~5% after hot CPI, and Brent fell over $20/bbl from last month's highs, yet both remain above their June lows, so the pullbacks haven't reversed the broader repricing of macro risk. VIX is finding support near 20, reversing its slide to ~14 in August; MOVE has held near 90, the 85th percentile over one year. Oil and Treasury positioning near year-to-date lows and oversold momentum argue for stabilization, but positioning exhaustion isn't fundamentals repricing. The post-midterm five-sigma equity drawdown resembles April 2025's tariff shock but arrives with inflation hotter (headline CPI estimated above 4% y/y in October), so Fed flexibility that cushioned past declines is less available, and Waller and Logan have turned more hawkish. A weaker post-midterm incentive for Trump's administration to counter equity weakness challenges the Fed put and the Trump put, making dip-buying harder as selloffs persist. A cross-asset vol composite nears April 2025 levels; MOVE just ended a 32-session streak above 90, the fifth-longest since 2020; and realized S&P volatility is set for its largest weekly gain this year, challenging the downtrend that had rewarded short-volatility strategies.
